admission.justification: Publishing through an old copied question list can silently erase another author’s question, and loading authority settings from a different coordination root can publish to the wrong task plane. The keyed task-owner edit and the separate loaded-root refusal jointly prevent those distinct costly misattributions.

applicability: Raised reconsideration questions published to a canonical leaf task document through the knowledge-ingest CLI question port and task owner.
conditions: Each supplied question has a nonempty key and text beginning with that key; all supplied fields validate before the keyed list mutation.

The task owner performs keyed insertion/rewording against the task document read inside its own publication transaction; the port does not republish its earlier copied question list, so unrelated intervening questions remain.

The lazy CLI port loads authority settings and compares resolved coordination roots before constructing TaskDocOpenQuestions; missing authority or a mismatched root gives an unavailable/refusing port.
exclusions: The loaded-root check is the CLI port-acquisition boundary, not an independent check by TaskDocOpenQuestions or an ongoing settings-file watcher.

This preserves other questions within the task owner transaction; it does not promise distributed/crash durability, undo already-published task questions after a memory-file failure, or certify an executed concurrency test.
statement: Raised questions must be inserted or reworded by keyed task-document publication without dropping concurrent questions and must refuse a mismatched loaded coordination root.
